clauses.reason: Terminated by own terms: section 1 closes the agencies on "Thursday, January 25, 1973" and section 2 only excepts offices from the first sentence of section 1, so both operate on that day alone; the end is recorded as 1973-01-25 inclusive (through the end of that day). Actor: EO:11700 itself. Nothing held revokes or amends the order.

research_rationale:
EO:11700 (signed 1973-01-23; 38 FR 2325, Federal Register of January 24, 1973) closes the executive departments, independent establishments and other governmental agencies, including field services, on "Thursday, January 25, 1973" as a mark of respect for Lyndon Baines Johnson, treats that day as within 5 U.S.C. 6103(b) and the statutes on compensation and leave (section 1), and provides that the first sentence of section 1 does not apply to offices the agency heads determine should remain open (section 2). Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing in jobs/fr-originals; number, date and subject agree with the census register. Inventory: the dossier's one clause covers sections 1 and 2, the complete operative text. Both sections operate only on that one day, so the order ends by its own terms on 1973-01-25, recorded inclusive (through the end of that day). Searches, chosen after reading their coverage notes (all complete, none with a coverage warning): the U.S. Code search (release point 119-121, citations of the order by number in statute text and notes; edition current through 2026-10-09) recorded 0 hits; the eCFR point-in-time search as of 2026-10-14 with GovInfo CFR bulk XML recorded 0 hits; the Federal Register catalog disposition-note search (1937 onward) recorded 0 hits for this order. I also searched every held order text (the Cruden held-text search, 33118 readable files) for the order's number; the only held texts that cite it are its own Federal Register printing. I found no held order that revokes or amends it.
